purpose: Cefepime is an antibiotic used to fight serious bacterial infections in your body. It can treat infections in your lungs, urinary tract, skin, and bloodstream. It is also used for infections that may happen when your immune system is weakened.
how_it_works: Cefepime works by attacking the outer wall that surrounds bacteria, which bacteria need to survive. Think of it like punching holes in the bacteria's protective shell. Without that shell, the bacteria fall apart and die, helping your body clear the infection.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects include pain or redness at the injection site, headache, nausea, diarrhea, rash, and itching. Some people may also notice a low-grade fever or mild stomach upset. These effects are usually temporary.
warnings: Tell your doctor if you are allergic to penicillin or any other antibiotic, because there is a small chance of a related allergic reaction. In rare cases, cefepime can affect the brain and cause confusion, seizures, or unusual movements, especially in patients with kidney problems or who receive too high a dose. Make sure your doctor knows about all your health conditions and medications before starting this drug.
typical_dosing: Cefepime is given by injection or IV drip in a hospital or clinic setting — it cannot be taken by mouth as a pill. The usual adult dose is 1 to 2 grams given every 8 to 12 hours, depending on the type and severity of your infection. Your doctor will adjust the dose if you have kidney problems. Treatment usually lasts 7 to 14 days.
